newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's PP to sue Gonzalez over corruption hints.
newsitem.headline: Spain's PP to sue Gonzalez over corruption hints.

text.p: Spain's ruling Popular Party (PP) said on Tuesday it will take legal action against opposition leader Felipe Gonzalez in an attempt to force him to confirm or deny reports that he accused the PP of corruption in its 1996 election campaign.
"The lawsuit...will be presented so that Gonzalez, as representative of his party, will confirm before a judge whether he made those statements," a PP spokeswoman told Reuters.

Spanish newspapers had quoted former prime minister Gonzalez as telling members of his Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE) in a closed-door meeting on February 8 that the PP received a $25 million campaign contribution from Emilio Azcarraga, chairman of Mexican media conglomerate Grupo Televisa.
Televisa has a 25 percent stake in a group led by domestic telephone company Telefonica to operate a hotly debated second digital television platform in Spain.

Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's conservative government has been accused by critics of hindering the first digital platform operator to ease the way for competition from a second operator, the Telefonica group.
Gonzalez has refused to confirm or deny the accusations against the PP publicly.
"It's absurd because all of this is based on something someone said Gonzalez said," a Socialist party spokeswoman said.

Gonzalez was prime minister for 13 years until the PP ousted him in the 1996 general election. His government was discredited by a series of scandals, including illegal campaign financing and running a "dirty war" against the Basque separatist group ETA.
The PP ran its election campaign on a "clean hands" platform which emphasised corruption in the Socialists' ranks.
